first_impression.reaction: Didn't expect this from a wedding blog. 'Most guides to Turkish wedding traditions list these customs in no particular order and repeat folklore as fact' is a big claim, but then they say they'll mark what's sourced and what's 'simply often told'. If they actually do that, I'll keep reading. I jumped to the FAQ and the legal section first, like I always do, and they held up.

journey.quote: This one follows the wedding in order and marks which details are sourced and which are simply often told.
journey.reaction: Good. That's the promise I'll hold them to. Most sites don't even try.

journey.section: The coffee at the asking, and the salt that is often told
journey.quote: Often told, though we found no cultural or academic source for it, is the story that the groom's cup is salted and he must drink it without complaint.
journey.reaction: Every other site states the salt coffee thing as gospel. Saying they couldn't source it is the most credible line on the page.

journey.quote: That is one region's example, but the lesson travels: leave room between the first visit and any engagement date.
journey.reaction: Fair. They're upfront that the evidence comes from one region's study, Hatay, and they don't stretch it to cover the whole country.

journey.quote: We did not find a cultural or academic source for its details in time for this guide, so we leave the specifics to your families, who will know how they do it.
journey.reaction: Honest, but 'in time for this guide' reads like they ran out of time. The gold pinning is the thing guests actually ask about, and here it's a shrug. I'd rather see it sourced than skipped.

journey.quote: We found no source on its meaning, so we will only say: when the line forms, your Australian guests should join it.
journey.reaction: Fine. Honest. A bit thin, but I'd take thin over made up.

journey.section: Marrying legally in Türkiye as an Australian
journey.quote: At Beyoğlu, the couple must attend the application together on a weekday, between 9am and 12pm or 1pm and 4.30pm, or appoint a proxy with a specific power of attorney that includes a photo.
journey.reaction: Specific hours, a named office, and a clear note that other offices may differ. That's the kind of detail I can check, and that's what I want.

journey.section: Marrying legally in Türkiye as an Australian
journey.quote: No fee is listed on the page.
journey.reaction: Good that they say so and don't guess a number. I still don't know what it costs, but I know why.

journey.quote: the page was updated on 30 October 2026.
journey.reaction: Dated and sourced to Smartraveller. That's the trust signal I look for.

journey.quote: If you would rather hand the paperwork timeline to one person, [speak with a Wedded Advisor](/wonderland-concierge), who stays with you from the first idea to the last dance.
journey.reaction: There it is, the pitch. At least it comes after the evidence, not before. But 'from the first idea to the last dance' is a slogan. It doesn't tell me what the advisor actually does, what it costs, or whether you take a cut from venues.

journey.section: Bringing Turkish traditions into your celebration
journey.quote: When you are ready to talk dates, documents and where in Türkiye your families will gather, your Wedded Advisor is a conversation away.
journey.reaction: Soft and not pushy, which I don't mind. Still no catch spelled out, so I'm not clicking yet.

unanswered_questions: What does a Wedded Advisor actually do for the legal paperwork? Do they lodge documents, book the marriage office, or just give me a checklist?
Is the Wedded Advisor service free, a flat fee, or a percentage? Do you take a commission from venues or suppliers?
Have you actually run a wedding in Türkiye for an Australian couple? Show me a real one with the actual budget.
How long before the date should the CNI and apostille process start? The page says 'well before you fly' but gives no weeks.
What does the takı töreni actually involve, and roughly what do guests give? You said you couldn't source it.

turn_offs_found.quote: who stays with you from the first idea to the last dance.
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional slogan doing the selling, with no detail on scope, fee or how independent the advice is. Everything else on the page is careful and sourced, so this stands out.

turn_offs_found.quote: our guide to [Turkish wedding destinations](/spotlight-on-turkish-wedding-destinations-the-best-places-to-tie-the-knot) is a good start.
turn_offs_found.why: Minor. The linked page's title says 'the best places', which is the kind of unsupported superlative I distrust. The sentence itself is fine.

would_share_with: My fiancée's family, for the legal section and the timeline of customs
Maybe a Reddit thread, for the fact that it says which customs it couldn't source

cta_reaction.quote: If you would rather hand the paperwork timeline to one person, [speak with a Wedded Advisor](/wonderland-concierge), who stays with you from the first idea to the last dance.
cta_reaction.why: The article earned some trust, so I'd click through to see the concierge page. I'm not enquiring until I see what the fee buys and whether there are supplier commissions. I don't expect a blog post to cover that, but the CTA line should at least say concretely what the advisor handles.

top_3_changes: Rewrite the Wedded Advisor CTA line to say concretely what the advisor does with the paperwork (e.g. the document checklist and marriage office timeline) and drop the 'first idea to the last dance' slogan.
Give a rough lead time for the CNI and apostille steps, sourced or marked to verify, so 'well before you fly' becomes something I can plan against.
Either source the takı töreni or remove 'in time for this guide', which reads like the job wasn't finished.
